earliest_visible_sign.description: Minute pale green, white, or yellow circular flecks on the youngest newly expanding leaves

characteristic_sign_or_lesion.description: Narrow broken or continuous chlorotic streaks running parallel to leaf veins, commonly more visible along secondary and tertiary veins.

secondary: red or reddish in some isolates
colors.color_progression: pale green, white, or yellow flecks elongate into yellow or white streaks, sometimes with red pigmentation

shape.shape_progression: tiny pale circular flecks elongate along secondary and tertiary veins into broken streaks, which merge into continuous stripes

size.size_variation_note: Streaks can fuse laterally into longer stripes covering much of the leaf

advanced_or_severe_stage.description: Severe stunting, shortened leaves, and abnormal ear development.
advanced_or_severe_stage.coalescence: Streaks merge and may extend over much of each new leaf.
advanced_or_severe_stage.tissue_death_appearance: Stunting and possible plant death if infected early.
secondary_signs: small, misshapen, poorly filled, or barren ears
abnormal bunching of shoots or flowers
advanced_or_severe_stage.percentage_affected_tissue_note: Streaks can cover most of newly formed leaves in severe cases.

distribution_on_plant.vertical_pattern: Symptoms occur primarily on leaves that emerge after infection; older leaves formed before infection may remain healthy.
distribution_on_plant.horizontal_pattern: Streaks extend along secondary and tertiary veins.
distribution_on_plant.other_parts_if_severe: Growing point (curved/abnormal apical growth) and ears/cobs.

pathognomonic_features: Minute pale green, white, or yellow circular flecks on the youngest newly expanding leaves.
Narrow broken or continuous yellow/white chlorotic streaks running parallel to secondary and tertiary leaf veins.
